title: Monoidal infinity Yoneda embedding and full faithfulness on operadic diagrams
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, universes and nonsymmetric monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small monoidal infinity category; no colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed. Write $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ for $\mathcal U'$-small spaces and $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$, formed in $\mathcal U''$. Equip this presheaf category with Day convolution: its tensor is the left Kan extension of $(F,G)\mapsto((c,d)\mapsto F(c)\times G(d))$ along $(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Here left Kan extension means the functor whose maps into a target functor correspond naturally to maps from the original functor into its restriction. Then $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ is presentably monoidal relative to $\mathcal U'$. The Yoneda functor $j(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)$ has a fully faithful strong monoidal enhancement
$$j^\otimes:\mathcal C^\otimes\longrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal C)^\otimes$$
over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with coherent equivalences $j(c)\otimes j(d)\simeq j(c\otimes d)$ and $j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})\simeq\mathbf1_{\mathcal P(\mathcal C)}$. Fully faithful means equivalence on every mapping space, and strong monoidal means preserving all cocartesian edges. For every $\mathcal U'$-small simplicial set $K$ and fixed map $a:K\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, postcomposition induces a fully faithful functor
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal C^\otimes)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal P(\mathcal C)^\otimes).$$
Here the source and target are coherent functors with the specified composite $a$ and transformations over its identity. For any specified collection $I$ of edges of $K$ whose images under $a$ are inert, the same assertion holds on the full subcategories of functors carrying every edge of $I$ to a cocartesian edge over its inert base arrow. All these comparisons are natural under precomposition in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.1.10 with K empty and K-prime all small shapes, in the associative-monoidal case, and Variant 4.8.1.11 (printed pp.710-711); the Day-convolution description of Remark 4.8.1.13 applies with associative rather than symmetric structure. Gepner-Haugseng 1312.3178v4, proof of Theorem 5.6.6 explicitly uses this monoidal Yoneda embedding and the induced fully faithful algebra inclusion. Full faithfulness on coherent diagrams is the fully faithful postcomposition property, using the full-subcategory model of functor categories; restriction to inert-preserving objects is full. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] with its small universe equal to $\mathcal U'$ and with no prescribed cocones. Its explicit localization model has no maps to invert, so it is exactly $P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$, with $j$ the Yoneda functor. It is presentable relative to $\mathcal U'$. For every finite $r$, its finite-variable assertion gives an equivalence between separately $\mathcal U'$-colimit-preserving functors $P^r\to P$ and functors $\mathcal C^r\to P$, including their coherent transformations and higher simplices; for $r=0$ both sides are $P$. The presheaf categories are formed in $\mathcal U''$; for the classifying category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ in step 2 one may use an additional ambient universe containing them. This changes none of the colimit shapes, which remain $\mathcal U'$-small. In particular this use requires no colimits or preservation hypothesis on $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Example 5.3.6.4 and Proposition 5.3.6.11; agent expansion of the empty-relation case.

proof.text: Write $m_r:\mathcal C^r\to\mathcal C$ for the reduced-input planar operations of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Step 1 extends $jm_r$ to separately cocontinuous $M_r:P^r\to P$ with $M_rj^r\simeq jm_r$. Take $M_0=j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$ and $M_1=\mathrm{id}_P$. The finite-variable restriction equivalences, including $r=0$, are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-coef-planar-multilinear-extension], with $A=\mathcal C$, $B=P$ and $f=j$. That lemma supplies the planar substitution equivalences and every tree-indexed higher compatibility, with the specified vertex comparisons. All lifting occurs on the reduced external input list, where every tree composite is separately cocontinuous. No restriction on functors with unused input variables is asserted.

source.place: Returned step 2: extend reduced planar operations and lift their substitution data.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with opposite $a:[m]\to[n]$, form the $i$th transport component by pulling $M_{a(i)-a(i-1)}$ back to the input block $a(i-1)+1,\ldots,a(i)$. Pull back the reduced-tree coherences of step 2 along the specified projections of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Its converse constructs a coherent classifying diagram with fibers $P^n$, and the comparisons $M_rj^r\simeq jm_r$ give a transformation with components $j^n$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] these unstraighten to $P^\otimes$ and a functor $j^\otimes$ preserving all cocartesian edges. Use the normal-form equivalence of the original $\mathcal C^\otimes$ to obtain this enhancement on the original source. Inert transports are coordinate projections and the $[0]$ fiber is terminal. For the relative inert-limit condition of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the object case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the mapping space over a base arrow into a tuple in $P^m$ with the product of its component mapping spaces, via the inert projections. For $m=0$ the product is a point. Thus the structure has the stated monoidal convention. Its tensor is $M_2$, which preserves small colimits separately, and its unit is $M_0=j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$.

source.place: Returned step 2: specified projection pullbacks and cocartesian unstraightening.

proof.text:
For $c,d\in\mathcal C$, tensoring arrows gives the coherent presheaf transformation $j(c)\boxtimes j(d)\to j(c\otimes d)\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The right-pinched mapping simplicial set of a product is degreewise the product, so $j(c)\boxtimes j(d)$ is represented by $(c,d)$. Apply evaluation in [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] to $\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal C$. Composition with this transformation identifies both mapping spaces with $H(c\otimes d)$:
$$\operatorname{Map}_P(j(c\otimes d),H)\simeq H(c\otimes d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(\mathcal C\times\mathcal C)}(j(c)\boxtimes j(d),H\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The comparison evaluates at the two identity arrows and is coherent in $c,d,H$.

source.place: Returned step 3: representable evaluation for the canonical Kan unit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-multilinear-presheaf-kan-recognition] with $r=2$, $A_1=A_2=D=\mathcal C$, $t=\otimes_{\mathcal C}$ and $E=M_2$. The separately cocontinuous hypothesis and specified representable comparisons are supplied by step 2. Its unit restricts to the tensor-of-arrows map of step 4, and its mapping-space equivalence for all $F,G,H$ is exactly the left Kan extension universal property in the item. This identifies the tensor with Day convolution, including its universal transformation. Apply the same lemma for every positive $r$ with $t=m_r$ and $E=M_r$. At $r=0$ its hypothesis is exactly $M_0=j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$; it gives the Kan extension of the point presheaf along the functor selecting the unit. No nonempty or filtered density diagram is assumed.

source.place: Returned step 3: general finite-arity density/Kan recognition, including the unit.

proof.text: For a planar tree with $r$ reduced external inputs, its composite operations preserve colimits in each input: an external variable enters exactly one subtree at each vertex; nullary vertices contribute fixed arguments. Their comparisons on representables are the original planar comparisons. Full faithfulness of the finite-variable restriction equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] identifies their comparison spaces and higher simplices with those used in step 2. The units in step 5 have the same prescribed restrictions, so their compatible comparison data are these lifts; uniqueness is also part of [lem-coef-planar-multilinear-extension]. For $r=0$ restriction is the identity on $P$. For base-arrow chains having discarded inputs, pull back these identified reduced comparisons along the specified projections of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Hence the operations, substitution and unit data of step 3 have the Day Kan description, with no fullness assertion after adding unused variables. By step 1 and separate cocontinuity of $M_2$, this is presentably monoidal; $j^\otimes$ has the required coherent tensor and unit equivalences.

source.place: Returned step 3: compatibility of reduced-tree comparisons and their specified projection pullbacks.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $j$ is fully faithful. Hence so is $j^n:\mathcal C^n\to P^n$ for every $n$: the right-pinched mapping simplicial set of a product is degreewise the product of the component mapping simplicial sets, and for $n=0$ it is a point. For objects $x$ over $[n]$, $y$ over $[m]$ and a base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, the $K=\Delta^0$ case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the homotopy fiber of the total mapping space over $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^\otimes_{[m]}}(\alpha_!x,y)$, and gives the same formula in $P^\otimes$. Since $j^\otimes$ preserves cocartesian edges, these formulas identify its map on these fibers with the fully faithful fiber map $j^m$, using $j^m(\alpha_!x)\simeq\alpha_!j^n(x)$. The mapping space of the base is the discrete set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}([n],[m])$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] over the identity of this base space: equivalence on every homotopy fiber proves equivalence of the total mapping spaces. Thus $j^\otimes$ is fully faithful as a functor of total infinity categories, not just on its fiber over $[1]$.

source.place: Dual of Proposition 2.4.4.2 and cocartesian mapping-space criterion; agent expansion to total mapping spaces.

proof.text: Factor $j^\otimes$ through its full replete essential image $R\subseteq P^\otimes$. Step 7 and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] give a coherent quasi-inverse for $\mathcal C^\otimes\to R$ with unit and counit equivalences. Every isomorphism of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is an identity: an order-preserving bijection of a finite ordinal fixes its successive elements. Apply [lem-coef-equivalence-over-gaunt-nerve] to this equivalence and the specified projections to $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$. The inverse and both equivalences are over the fixed base, as simplicial maps and transformations.

source.place: Returned step 5: full essential image and strict-base inverse.

proof.text: The essential image $R$ is stable under cocartesian transport. Indeed step 8 gives, for each $z\in R$, an equivalence $z\simeq j^\otimes(x)$ over the identity of its base object. Transport is a coherent functor by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], so sends this to $\alpha_!z\simeq\alpha_!j^\otimes(x)\simeq j^\otimes(\alpha_!x)$; the second equivalence uses preservation of cocartesian edges from step 3. Repleteness puts the endpoint in $R$. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-full-restriction]: $R\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cocartesian and, for every fixed $a:K\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, its relative functor category is a quasicategory and a full subcategory of the corresponding category for $P^\otimes$.

For the fixed $a:K\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, postcompose the inverse data of step 8. By [lem-coef-equivalence-over-gaunt-nerve] this gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal C^\otimes)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,R)$. These are quasicategories by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] and step 9. A functor equivalence induces mapping-space equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-full-restriction], the inclusion into the relative functor category for $P^\otimes$ has identical right-pinched mapping simplicial sets between retained objects. Composing gives full faithfulness over the specified base diagram $a$.

source.place: Returned step 5: strict relative diagram equivalence followed by full inclusion.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the specified inert-labelled edges. Step 3 shows that postcomposition with $j^\otimes$ carries a functor taking these edges to cocartesian edges to another such functor. Both restrictions in the item are full subcategories on their specified objects: no condition is imposed on transformations. Therefore the mapping spaces between any two retained objects are unchanged, and the equivalences proved in step 10 restrict to these mapping spaces. Finally, every comparison in steps 10-11 is induced by postcomposition with the single functor $j^\otimes$; for a simplicial map $u:L\to K$ the equality $(j^\otimes F)u=j^\otimes(Fu)$ holds in every simplicial degree. This proves naturality under precomposition, with base map $au$ and the pulled-back specified edge condition.

source.place: Agent proof: restriction to full subcategories and degreewise associativity of precomposition.
